text:
Anika: quick sync — we hit a conflict where private VPC policy forbids egress that hosted expects for telemetry. need a contract for routing/credential precedence. cc @Jonah
Jonah: are we talking about KMS/secret access or network NAT egress?
Anika: both. the private control plane hides the runtime creds; hosted wants telemetry / metrics -> ingestion endpoint. this breaks onboarding for a few enterprise customers.
Maria: short term we used a proxy token exchange for cust-42. worked but brittle and manual. not scalable.
Leo: Proposal A: precedence table. customer-managed (private) policies win for hard denies; platform-managed rules (hosted/dedicated) can request exceptions via an auditable approval flow.
Jonah: Proposal B: add a translation gateway that maps a private deny/allow into a minimal outbound facade with observability hooks. gateway needs cert pinning + limited scope.
SRE-Bot: deploy-check: customer-42: blocked egress to telemetry.redwood.ai (policy deny) — failing healthchecks.
Anika: sketch compromise: default precedence = private-deny wins. allow an "audit-approved" short-lived exchange token to open specific minimal egress (ttl small, very constrained scope).
Maria: rough token-exchange sketch:
```
POST /v1/bridge/exchange
{ "customer": "cust-42", "target": "telemetry", "scope": ["metrics:ingest"], "ttl": 300 }
```
Jonah: who mints the token? control plane? private control plane must either mint or sign, otherwise we risk secret sharing.
Leo: avoid cross-control-plane secret copying. have private control plane mint and sign the token; platform verifies signature against a discovered public key set.
Anika: good. that keeps private keys in customer boundary. we need pubkey discovery + rotation, plus audit fields embedded in token (requested-by, reason, approval-id).
Maria: also add an observable fallback: if telemetry blocked, runtime buffers metrics locally and ships when allowed or via customer-controlled sink. document invariants (max buffer size, data retention).
Jonah: I'll draft the threat model section (replay, forged tokens, scope escalation).
Anika: next steps: I will draft an RFC for the "token-bridge" pattern — include: token schema, TTL, scope semantics, audit trail, pubkey discovery, failure modes, and metrics.
Leo: I'll own key rotation and pubkey discovery mechanics (JWKS or similar).
Maria: I'll own buffering semantics and fallback playbook.
Jonah: I'll own threat model + verification checklist.
Anika: thanks all. action items summarized: @Jonah threat model, @Maria buffering/fallback, @Leo key rotation/pubkey discovery, @Anika RFC + prototype. aim to land a prototype next sprint. :rocket:
